key_insight: A remote, model-based memory test can produce a stable individual score that tracks memory dysfunction over time in older adults.
clinical_relevance: This approach could enable frequent, scalable monitoring of early cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment and healthy aging without requiring in-person testing.
method: 51 older adults (24 with amnestic mild cognitive impairment, 27 healthy controls) completed weekly 8-minute unsupervised online memory assessments for up to 1 year.
Responses were fit to a formal memory consolidation and forgetting model to generate an individualized Seattle-Groningen Memory Assessment (SGMA) score.
The score was evaluated for reliability, practice effects, stability across materials, and diagnostic performance.
evidence_signal: The SGMA score showed mean reliability of r = 0.70 across assessments, minimal practice effects (~0.2% increase per assessment), and up to 87% accuracy for detecting mild cognitive impairment.
watch_item: The sample was small and relatively well-characterized, so broader validation is needed before routine deployment across more diverse populations and home testing conditions.
paper_title: Detection and Continuous Monitoring of Memory Dysfunction in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Healthy Aging Through Adaptive Computational Phenotyping
